title: Constrained Look-ahead Guidance for Interference-Aware Flow Editing
claim: Greedy edit-then-project updates can get trapped in infeasible optima, while look-ahead probing of both objectives reaches the feasible optimum.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, shared legend below, dashed divider
description: Two side-by-side 2-D toy landscapes, titled 'Edit-first + projection' on the left and 'Look-ahead' on the right, separated by a dashed vertical line. Each panel has purple contour lines around two edit maxima (stars labeled A and B) and a green dashed circle, the fidelity basin, centered on the source point x^src. In the left panel, a red arrow from x_k heads toward infeasible maximum A, then an orange dashed projection arrow pulls it back toward the basin. In the right panel, a purple dashed edit probe and a green dashed fidelity probe combine into a black look-ahead arrow that moves toward feasible maximum B inside the basin. Legends for arrows, stars, basin and A/B feasibility sit at the bottom and left. The eye goes to the arrows and contours first.
caption: Mechanism comparison. Left: edit-first update moves along gedit but may violate fidelity constrain and need projects back to the fidelity basin. Right: the look-ahead update uses edit and fidelity probes to evaluate ∇xLLA before committing an update, steering the trajectory toward the feasible edit maximum inside the fidelity basin.
abstract: Diffusion and flow models enable powerful generative modeling, but controlled editing remains challenging due to the need to balance source fidelity and edit compliance along the generative trajectory. We propose a principled, inversion-free framework for flow-based image editing from a trajectory centric perspective. Rather than relying on inversion or heuristic guidance, we introduce a one-step look-ahead mechanism that evaluates the effect of candidate updates on both edit and fidelity rewards estimated via denoising, and adjusts the current update based on this evaluation. At each step, our method applies reward-driven corrections guided by the look-ahead evaluation under an explicit fidelity constraint, resulting in stable and coherent trajectory evolution. This look-ahead design mitigates gradient interference between edit and fidelity objectives by anticipating their interaction in future states, leading to improved trade-offs. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves stronger semantic edits while better preserving source content compared to existing strong baselines.
